title: Budgeted Active Experimentation for Treatment Effect Estimation from Observational and Randomized Data
claim: An iterative loop scores unlabeled candidates with a multi-criteria acquisition function, runs randomized trials on the top picks, and retrains the learner.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right then looping back, dashed feedback arrow
description: A single flow diagram with color-coded boxes joined by black arrows. At top left, a blue-outlined box (accumulated RCT data) and an orange box (observational data) merge into a bracket labeled 'Calibrate Confounding' and 'Abundant Supervision'. The merged arrow feeds a dashed gray 'CATE Learner Model' region that holds two blue-gray boxes, Representation Learning (φ) and CATE Estimator (τ̂). Output from the estimator goes down into a purple diamond, the Multi-Criteria Acquisition Function S(u). Three green boxes (epistemic uncertainty, domain discrepancy, overlap deficit) and a gray dashed 'Unlabeled Candidate Pool' box feed the diamond. From the diamond the flow goes down to 'Select Top-m_k Batch', then 'Execute RCT & Observe Outcomes'. A blue dashed 'Adaptive Dataset Update' arrow returns to the RCT data box. The purple diamond is the visual center.
caption: Overview of the proposed Budgeted Active Experimentation framework for OBS-RCT fusion. We first train a CATE learner using abundant observational logs, then iteratively select a small batch of units from an unlabeled candidate pool Dpool for randomized experiments under a fixed budget. At each iteration, a multi-criteria acquisition function S(u) scores and ranks candidates by balancing three signals: epistemic uncertainty (vu), domain discrepancy (du), and overlap deficit (ou). We select the top-ranked units to run RCTs, add the new outcomes to the labeled set, and update the learner to reduce CATE estimation error.
abstract: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects is central to data-driven decision-making, yet industrial applications often face a fundamental tension between limited randomized controlled trial (RCT) budgets and abundant but biased observational data collected under historical targeting policies. Although observational logs offer the advantage of scale, they inherently suffer from severe policyinduced imbalance and overlap violations, rendering standalone estimation unreliable. We propose a budgeted active experimentation framework that iteratively enhances model training for causal effect estimation via active sampling. By leveraging observational priors, we develop an acquisition function targeting uplift estimation uncertainty, overlap deficits, and domain discrepancy to select the most informative units for randomized experiments. We establish finite-sample deviation bounds, asymptotic normality via martingale Central Limit Theorems (CLTs), and minimax lower bounds to prove information-theoretic optimality. Extensive experiments on industrial datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms standard randomized baselines in cost-constrained settings.
